area: Dashboard layout width: (1) page-level max-width cap on the operator dashboard shell, (2) extending the 68ch `.prose-measure` cap to dashboard free-text surfaces
summary: The premise "read app/[locale]/dashboard/layout.tsx" is wrong: no dashboard layout.tsx exists anywhere in the app tree. The dashboard shell is a per-page-imported client component, components-legacy/dashboard/DashboardLayout.tsx, wrapped manually by 44 of 49 dashboard pages; 5 pages bypass it entirely. Its content chain (lines 287 -> 431 -> 473) carries zero max-w classes, so `<main>` at line 473 is the single correct insertion point for change 1. The 64px sidebar is `position: fixed` (line 289), sitting entirely OUTSIDE the capped container, with the content column offset by `md:ml-[64px]` (line 431) — so a cap plus `mx-auto` centres content inside the region right of the rail, which is what you want. For change 2, `.prose-measure { max-width: 68ch }` already exists at app/globals.css:224-226 inside `@layer utilities`, is live on 9 customer surfaces, and has zero dashboard usages. Two things contradict the brief: LOCKFILE.md references a "Dashboard content max-width row above" three times (lines 437, 439, 443) but that row does not exist in the container-widths table at lines 939-947, so no width value is actually locked; and there is no email-template editor in the dashboard at all (templates are server-side generators in lib/email-templates/).

findings.claim: No app/[locale]/dashboard/layout.tsx exists. The entire app tree contains exactly 5 layout files, none under dashboard, and no route groups under dashboard either.
findings.evidence: `find app -name 'layout.tsx'` returns only: app/layout.tsx, app/[locale]/layout.tsx, app/[locale]/partner/layout.tsx, app/[locale]/salon/[slug]/layout.tsx, app/[locale]/dev/flows/layout.tsx. `find app -name 'layout.tsx' -path '*dash*'` returns nothing. `find app/[locale]/dashboard -type d -name '(*)'` returns nothing.

findings.claim: The dashboard shell is components-legacy/dashboard/DashboardLayout.tsx, imported and wrapped MANUALLY by each page. 44 of 49 dashboard pages use it; 5 do not.

Usage e.g. app/[locale]/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx:653, analytics/page.tsx:143, settings/page.tsx:1476. Per-file loop over all 49 page.tsx: the 5 without it are editor, messages, gallery, setup, queue-display.

findings.claim: CHANGE 1 TARGET. The shell's content chain has zero max-w. `<main>` at DashboardLayout.tsx:473 is the only correct insertion point: `<main className="flex-1 px-4 pt-6 pb-10 sm:px-6 md:py-8">`

findings.claim: ANSWER TO Q5: the sidebar sits OUTSIDE the container being capped. It is `position: fixed`, therefore out of normal flow; the content column reserves space with `md:ml-[64px]`. A cap applied at :473 therefore centres content within the viewport-minus-64px region, not the full viewport.

findings.claim: Nested <main> landmark violation, pre-existing and unrelated to but touched by change 1. Every dashboard page renders a <main> inside the locale layout's <main>.
findings.evidence: app/[locale]/layout.tsx:114 `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} className="pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)] isolate">` wraps {children} at :118. components-legacy/dashboard/DashboardLayout.tsx:473 renders a second `<main>` inside it. gallery/page.tsx:56 does the same.

gaps.what: No locked value for the dashboard content max-width. LOCKFILE cites a 'Dashboard content max-width row' that was never written, and the research's suggested 1440px misquotes its own cited precedent (the locked /business hero is 1400px).
gaps.why_it_matters: Per taste rule 9 and global rule 1, an unlocked value must not be filled from memory. Picking 1440 vs 1400 vs 1280 is a one-word decision but it is the owner's, and it will be copied by every future dashboard surface. Shipping an invented number also re-creates the exact 'a fourth width nobody chose' problem the container-widths table exists to prevent.
gaps.existing_thing_to_extend: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md:939-947 Container widths table — add the missing Dashboard content row so the three dangling citations at :437/:439/:443 resolve.

gaps.what: The sticky topbar (DashboardLayout.tsx:433) is a sibling of <main> and stays full-bleed when <main> is capped. Its right-hand controls (search button :438, NotificationCenter :441) would then sit ~560px right of the content's right edge on a 2560px monitor.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the one thing a naive one-line cap gets visually wrong, and it is exactly the kind of 'unbalanced' result the owner rejects on sight. Two defensible answers exist: leave the bar viewport-pinned (consistent with the rail, which is also viewport-pinned chrome — this is what Fresha/Stripe do) or cap the bar's inner content to the same width, which needs an added wrapper div and is therefore no longer a one-line change. It should be shown in the mockup rather than decided silently.

gaps.what: 5 dashboard pages bypass DashboardLayout entirely, so a shell-level cap cannot reach them: editor, gallery, setup, queue-display, messages.
gaps.why_it_matters: Four are legitimately exempt (messages is a pure redirect; setup is a full-screen onboarding flow; queue-display is a full-bleed dark TV board; editor is the visual editor). Gallery is NOT intentional — it is missing the whole shell including the rail, which is a separate bug that a width sweep will make visible but not fix.
gaps.existing_thing_to_extend: app/[locale]/dashboard/gallery/page.tsx:56 — should be wrapped in DashboardLayout like the other 44 pages.

gaps.what: No enforcement for either change. Nothing measures dashboard content width at a wide viewport, and nothing checks that a new dashboard textarea reaches for .prose-measure.
gaps.why_it_matters: This estate's own retro concluded gates work and advice does not. Both rules will drift back on the next new dashboard page without a check. The research entry itself proposes a geometry rule: measure main content width at 1920px and fail if it equals viewport width minus only the fixed padding.
gaps.existing_thing_to_extend: scripts/check-geometry.mjs (already runs FLOORS passes at tablet 768x1024 and desktop 1280x900 per LOCKFILE:1930) — add a 1920px dashboard width assertion.

gaps.what: The dashboard calendar week view will lose real estate under any cap and has no named exemption.
gaps.why_it_matters: It defaults to the 8-column week grid and is the one surface where more width genuinely buys information. It will not break (overflow-x-auto plus min-w-[600px] already handle narrowing), but at a 1440 cap each day column lands around 165px versus about 310px unbounded on a 2560px screen. This needs to be a stated decision, not a side effect.

recommendation:
CHANGE 1 — exactly one line, one file. components-legacy/dashboard/DashboardLayout.tsx:473. Replace `<main className="flex-1 px-4 pt-6 pb-10 sm:px-6 md:py-8">` with `<main className="flex-1 w-full max-w-[1440px] mx-auto px-4 pt-6 pb-10 sm:px-6 md:py-8">`. Three notes on that string: `mx-auto` is load-bearing (without it the content hugs the 64px rail and dumps the entire slack into a single right gutter, about 1056px of dead space on a 2560px monitor, which is worse than no cap); `w-full` is needed because the element is a flex child, so `flex-1` alone plus a max-width is fine but `w-full` makes the intent explicit and survives a future `flex-col` refactor; and the 1440 value is NOT locked — see gaps, confirm it with the owner or write the LOCKFILE row first. This one line reaches 44 of 49 pages. Do NOT put the cap on line 431 (the column div) — that would cap the sticky topbar's white background too and leave sunken grey either side of it, which reads as broken.

CHANGE 2 — add the `prose-measure` class token to each site; no new CSS, the utility already exists at app/globals.css:224. Priority order, highest value first: (a) components-legacy/dashboard/SalonAboutEditor.tsx:121, the salon description editor, the single most important one; (b) app/[locale]/dashboard/help-editor/page.tsx:163, rows={10}, the longest body in the dashboard; (c) app/[locale]/dashboard/reviews/page.tsx:224, the read-only customer review comment, currently fully unbounded prose; (d) app/[locale]/dashboard/settings/page.tsx:164 and :170, description_de / description_en; (e) app/[locale]/dashboard/services/page.tsx:127 (editor) plus :609 and :610 (read-only service descriptions); (f) content-editor/page.tsx:94, discovery-admin/page.tsx:303, reports/page.tsx:253, refunds/page.tsx:232, approvals/page.tsx:176, upcharge/page.tsx:264, discovery-posts/page.tsx:180, reviews/page.tsx:260. It composes safely — `.prose-measure` sets only max-width, every target sets only `w-full`, and none carries a competing max-w-*.

SKIP in change 2: the short single-purpose note fields (reviews/page.tsx:304 flag reason, and the coiffeur/spa/nail/barber per-client note widgets at ConsultationNotes.tsx:142, FormulaBook.tsx:224, FormulaTab.tsx:119, WellnessJournal.tsx:280/294, TreatmentOutcome.tsx:120/125/136, FadeBlueprint.tsx:345, NailPreferencesForm.tsx:179). They are rows={2} inside already-narrow panels (several sit inside max-w-md containers), so the cap buys nothing and adds churn. Also drop "email templates" from the brief entirely — no such dashboard surface exists.

EXEMPT from change 1, name these explicitly: app/[locale]/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx (the 8-column week grid at :894-896 is the one surface where width buys information; either accept the narrowing, which is safe because overflow-x-auto plus min-w-[600px] already absorb it, or give the week/day view a named `max-w-none` opt-out — owner's call, show both in the mockup). Auto-exempt because they bypass the shell and need no edit: editor, setup, queue-display, messages. Gallery is auto-exempt for the same mechanical reason but that is a bug, not a decision — file it separately.

SEQUENCING. Write the LOCKFILE Dashboard content row at _design-system/LOCKFILE.md:947 in the same turn as the code change, so the three dangling citations at :437/:439/:443 stop pointing at nothing, and flip the two AWAITING OWNER lines in _plans/PRINCIPLES_LOOP.md and _plans/CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT.md. Both changes are visual and land on live operator surfaces, so the mockup-first rule binds: LOCKFILE:439 says so by name for change 2. Verify at 1920px and 2560px, not at 1280px, where a 1440 cap is invisible and would produce a false PASS.
